title: Ready, Set, Know!
description: A family-friendly general knowledge game covering animals, space, fast food, the human body, famous words, and world geography.

questions.question: This flightless black-and-white bird is an expert swimmer and proposes to its mate with a pebble.
This lizard changes color not just to hide, but also to communicate its mood.
Despite its towering height, the world's tallest animal has only seven neck bones — the same as a human.
This ocean mammal communicates using unique signature whistles that function like names within its group.
This Mexican salamander can regrow its limbs, spinal cord, and even parts of its own heart.
In July 1969, Neil Armstrong became the first human to walk on this natural satellite of Earth.
Home to Olympus Mons — the solar system's largest volcano — this is known as the Red Planet.
The Great Red Spot on this giant gas planet is a storm that has raged for hundreds of years.
Its first module launched in 1998, this orbiting laboratory circles Earth roughly every 90 minutes.
questions.answer: What is the International Space Station?

questions.question: Launched in 1977, this NASA probe became the first human-made object to reach interstellar space in 2012.
McDonald's introduced this kids' meal — complete with a toy — in 1979.
This red-haired, big-shoed clown has been the mascot of McDonald's since the 1960s.
Burger King's flagship sandwich has been its signature since 1957, originally selling for just 37 cents.
Founded by Truett Cathy in 1967, this chicken chain is the only major fast food restaurant closed every Sunday.
This West Coast burger chain officially calls its fan-favorite customizations the 'Not So Secret Menu.'
Working nonstop, this fist-sized muscle beats about 100,000 times every single day.
Weighing roughly 8 pounds and covering your entire body, this is your largest organ.
This thigh bone is the longest and strongest in the human body.
An adult human body contains about 5 liters of this oxygen-carrying tissue.
The only tissue in the body that gets no blood supply, drawing its oxygen directly from the air.
This boxing legend and Olympic champion coined the phrase 'Float like a butterfly, sting like a bee.'
Stepping onto the Moon in 1969, he declared, 'One small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.'
This U.S. president made 'Speak softly and carry a big stick' his signature foreign policy motto.
After newspapers wrongly reported his death in 1897, this humorist quipped, 'The report of my death was an exaggeration.'
His 1863 Gettysburg Address closed with a call for 'government of the people, by the people, for the people.'
Flowing north through Africa to the Mediterranean Sea, this is the world's longest river.
At 29,032 feet above sea level, this Himalayan peak is the highest point on Earth.
This saltwater lake on the Israel-Jordan border, over 1,400 feet below sea level, is Earth's lowest land point.
Spanning most of northern South America, this forest contains roughly half of all remaining rainforest on Earth.
At its narrowest, just 55 miles of open water separate Russia from Alaska in this cold arctic passage.
